blocks.text: The DNS64 prefix is an IPv6 address prefix used by Zscaler's purpose-built DNS64 mechanism to synthesize AAAA records from A records returned to servers that can be reached via IPv4. Zscaler facilitates the DNS64 mechanism with its own default IPv6 prefix and the well-known prefix (64:ff:9b::/96), without requiring any additional configurations by Internet & SaaS (ZIA) administrators. However, organizations can configure and use their network-specific DNS64 prefixes instead of the default prefixes supported by Zscaler. You can designate one of the configured NAT64 prefixes as the DNS64 prefix for your organization. You can also configure a DNS64 prefix for individual locations and override the global DNS64 prefix for those locations. To learn more, see Configuring Locations.
Zscaler's support for the DNS64 prefix provides the following benefits:

blocks.item: Enable synthesizing of AAAA records for IPv4 destinations using the DNS64 mechanism.
Allow flexibility in prefix selection for synthetic IPv6 addresses by supporting Zscaler's default prefix, the well-known prefix (64:ff9b::/96), and an organization's network-specific prefix.

blocks.text: DNS64 prefix selection by Zscaler from the prefixes available at different sources follows a specific order, as explained in the following list:

blocks.item: Customer-configured prefix for a location in the Zscaler Admin Console
Customer-configured prefix for an organization in the Zscaler Admin Console
Zscaler's default prefix for the cloud on which your organization is provisioned

blocks.text: To learn more, see Understanding IPv6 Support.
On the DNS64 Prefix page (Infrastructure > Internet & SaaS > IPv6 Configuration > DNS64 Prefix), you can do the following:

blocks.item: Configure a DNS64 prefix at the organization level.
Modify the table and its columns.
View the DNS64 prefix configured at the organization level. You can view:
Name: The name of the DNS64 prefix.
Prefix/Mask: The DNS64 prefix and the subnet mask for the prefix.
Description: The description of the DNS64 prefix.
Go to the NAT64 Prefixes and Settings pages.
